results.title: Money over merit: How vote-buying is threatening Ghana’s leadership and national development
results.content: Vote-buying in Ghana is increasingly becoming a major threat to democratic accountability and national development. What should be a process of electing leaders based on competence, integrity, experience and vision is gradually being influenced by money, gifts and other material inducements. Unfortunately, some Ghanaians have come to accept the distribution of money to delegates and voters as a normal part of political competition. This raises serious concerns about the quality of leadership the country is producing. One of the most worrying consequences is that capable individuals who genuinely have the knowledge, experience and commitment to deliver are increasingly at risk of being overlooked because they cannot compete financially. results.title: Türkiye formally adopts new name as part of official country branding strategy

results.title: Gold Fields says Tarkwa mine has contributed US$3.3bn to Ghana
results.content: Gold Fields Ghana Limited says it has paid US$3.3 billion to the Government of Ghana in royalties, corporate taxes and dividends from its operations at the Tarkwa mine. In a media statement issued on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, the company also disclosed that it had invested more than US$5 billion in developing and sustaining the mine. The statement comes as the government reviews the company's application to renew the Tarkwa mining leases. Gold Fields said it submitted the application in November 2025, following a request from the government to do so early. Gold Fields said it was among the mining companies invited to invest in Ghana in the early 1990s as part of efforts to revive the country's gold sector.
